get.description: Get a paginated collection of devices with filtering and sorting options.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Starting index for pagination (zero-based). If not provided, the default is 0.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return per page. If not provided, the default is 2000.

parameters.name: sortby
parameters.description:
Field to sort the results by.
Example: name(ascending).

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description:
Specific fields to include in the response (for partial responses). 
Example: fields=uuid && fields=name.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description:
Filter conditions to apply to the results. 
Example: filters = ((name contains sometext) and (uuid eq dummy-id)).

parameters.name: obj_uuids
parameters.description:
List of specific object UUIDs to retrieve. 
Example:  obj_uuids=uuid1 && obj_uuids=uuid2.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: When set to true, only returns the total count of matching resources without the actual resources.

allOf.description:
ListDevicesV1Response represents the response containing a list of devices and metadata.
This message provides both the device data and pagination information.

get.description: Retrieve a specific device by UUID. Fetches detailed information about a device using its unique identifier.

parameters.name: device_uuid
parameters.description:
device_uuid is the unique identifier of the device to retrieve.
This field is required and must be a valid UUID string.

allOf.description:
GetDeviceV1Response represents the response containing a single device's information.
This message is returned when a device is successfully retrieved.

description.description: Description is the user-provided description of the device.

management_state.description:
ManagementState indicates the current management status of the device.
Possible values:
  - DISCOVERY_NOT_INITIATED: Discovery process has not started.
  - ZTP_NOT_INITIATED: Zero Touch Provisioning has not started.
  - DISCOVERY_FAILED: Device discovery failed.
  - DEVICE_DETECTED: Device has been detected.
  - DISCOVERY_IN_PROGRESS: Discovery is currently in progress.
  - MANAGED: Device is managed by the system.
  - UNMANAGED: Device is not managed by the system.
  - MAINTENANCE: Device is in maintenance mode.
  - SALVAGE: Device is in salvage state.
  - SYNC_PENDING: Device synchronization is pending.
  - MISCONFIGURED: Device is misconfigured.

login_connection_state.description:
LoginConnectionState indicates the current connection status to the device.
Possible values:
  - UP: Connection to the device is established.
  - DOWN: Connection to the device is not established.

combined_state.description: CombinedState represents the overall operational state derived from management and connection states.

device_sync_status.description: DeviceSyncStatus indicates the synchronization status between the device and the system.

management_state_description.description: ManagementStateDescription provides a description of the management state.

reboot_time.description: RebootTime is the last reboot time of the device.

reboot_time_stamp.description: RebootTimeStamp is the timestamp of the last reboot.

device_config_state.description: DeviceConfigState describes whether the device contains out of band changes.

last_oob_syslog_timestamp.description: LastOobSyslogTimestamp is the time the last out of band syslog message was received for this device.

items.description: Items contains the complete information of the requested devices.

count.description:
Count represents the total number of devices that match the request criteria.
This count may be larger than the number of items in Devices if pagination is applied.
This field will be serialized as "count" in JSON format.

protobufAny.title: protobufAny

typeUrl.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

value.description: Must be a valid serialized protocol buffer of the above specified type.
